assertions.text: Precision after verification is at least 0.8
assertions.how: a grader who has not seen the run maps each confirmed finding that is not a deterministic tool finding to one seeded defect, to 'real but not seeded' (with the reason it is a genuine problem for these users), or to 'not a problem'; precision = (seeded + real but not seeded) / confirmed judged findings >= 0.8. Also report the strict precision, seeded / confirmed judged findings, and the recall by meaning

assertions.text: The reply puts the fixes in priority order and says what needs a person
assertions.how: the final reply lists the confirmed problems from most to least severe, or the P0/P1 first, and names what the agent could not check (needs-human WCAG items, real skippers)

findings.title: Clipped text in li:nth-of-type(1) > article.card > div.card__body > h2.card_
findings.description: Text ("Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries") overflows a box with overflow hidden at 320 px (scroll 327×46 vs client 184×46, axis x).

findings.title: Not reachable by keyboard: "Fernhill Tool Library"
findings.description: The a "Fernhill Tool Library" is tabbable in the DOM, but a complete Tab walk never reached it. People who use a keyboard or switch cannot operate it.

findings.title: Pick-up session options are shown in reverse date order while keyboard and screen-reader order runs forward
findings.description: Under 1.3.2, the reading order that assistive technology exposes should match the visual order when order affects meaning. On the basket page the DOM and ARIA order of the session radios is chronological, from Saturday 10 October to Wednesday 28 October. On screen the order is reversed at every width. At 320 px Wednesday 28 October is at the top and Saturday 10 October at the bottom. At 1280 px Wednesday 28 October spans the first row, then the second row runs right to left from Saturday 24 to Saturday 10. Arrow keys inside the radio group therefore move visually backwards, and a screen reader reads the dates in the opposite order to what sighted users see.

findings.title: Pick-up day chosen on the tool page is not pre-selected among the basket's sessions
findings.description: Members should not have to remember a choice they have just made. On the tool page the member picks a pick-up day (for example Saturday 17 October, which is a session), and the basket line repeats 'Pick up Saturday 17 October'. Yet the 'Pick-up session' radios start empty, and pressing Continue gives the error 'Choose a pick-up session'. The same date has to be found and chosen again from six options listed in reverse order. 3.3.7 is met narrowly, because the earlier answer is available to select, but the member still has to carry the choice across screens.

findings.title: Search with no matches shows the full tool list and announces nothing
findings.description: After a search, members should learn what happened. Searching 'ladder' writes '1 tool found' into the status region and filters the list, which works. Searching 'sewing machine' leaves the status region empty and the list showing all ten tools, with no 'no tools found' message on screen or in the live region (probe 45). Screen-reader users hear nothing, and sighted users see what looks like matching results.

findings.title: 'Reserve this tool' sits outside every landmark
findings.description: Under A11Y-26, primary content belongs inside a landmark. On the tool page the ARIA snapshot places button 'Reserve this tool' (in the fixed action bar) after main and before contentinfo, outside any landmark. Screen-reader users who move by landmarks, or who read main only, will not meet the page's primary action.

findings.title: Item headings share the level of their section heading on the find and basket pages
findings.description: Under A11Y-26, a heading nested inside a section ranks one level below the section heading. On the find page each tool card's heading is h2, the same level as the 'Tools' h2 that contains them. On the basket page the tool's heading is h2 under the 'Tools' h2. The heading list for screen-reader users is flat, so the cards look like peers of 'Search' and 'Opening times'.

findings.title: Dark-theme success token diverges from the declared value, giving the 'Available from' badge low text contrast
findings.description: design.md declares dark success #8fd1a8 and selection #24352c. styles.css sets dark --color-ok to #2f7d4a and --color-ok-tint to #1d2622 (the card surface). The .badge--ok text is therefore #2f7d4a on #1d2622, about 3.1:1 by the WCAG formula, for 16 px bold text, which needs 4.5:1; the badge background also equals the card surface, so the badge has no fill.

findings.title: Loan-length listbox captures Tab, cycling focus among its options
findings.description: Tab should leave a listbox. The keydown handler on #loan-list treats Tab like ArrowDown with preventDefault, so Tab (and Shift+Tab, which is not distinguished) moves to the next option forever; the only exits are choosing an option with Enter/Space or clicking.

findings.title: Loan-length button's accessible name omits the field label
findings.description: A select-like button should expose its label with its value. #loan-button's name is only its content ('One week'); the 'Loan length' heading is tied to the listbox (aria-labelledby on #loan-list) but not to the button, which is the control a screen reader meets.

findings.title: Calendar accepts closed days without warning
findings.description: All 21 day buttons can be chosen and Reserve accepts a closed day such as Monday 12 October (same as F-0065).

findings.title: Closed-day error appears only at final confirm, with no route back to the day
findings.description: After the details are filled in, Confirm shows 'The library is closed on Monday 12 October' as plain text with no link to change the day.

findings.title: Pick-up before the tool's available-from date is never checked
findings.description: A tool available from Sat 17 can be reserved and confirmed for Sat 10 (same as F-0066).

findings.title: Each tool's pick-up day and the basket's pick-up session are stored separately and never reconciled
findings.description: The flow asks for a pick-up day per tool on the tool page and again for one pick-up session on the basket page. The two are stored independently (basket item.day, URL slot) and nothing checks that they agree, so the confirm summary can say 'pick up Saturday 10 October' for a tool next to 'Pick-up session: Wednesday 28 October'.

findings.title: Continue and Confirm set aria-busy with no visible or disabled state while waiting
findings.description: A pressed button that starts a 1.2-1.5 s wait should show that it is working. The submit handlers set aria-busy on #continue and #confirm, but styles.css has no [aria-busy] rule and the buttons are not disabled, so nothing on screen changes until the page navigates or an error appears.

findings.title: Pressing Confirm again while waiting allocates a second reservation number
findings.description: A submit should be idempotent while pending. Each Confirm submit pushes a new reference (FT-4471, FT-4472, ...) into sessionStorage before the 1.5 s timer, and the button stays enabled, so a second press creates a second reservation for the same tools; the done page then lists 'Reservation numbers FT-4471 and FT-4472'.

findings.title: Done page reservation number comes from session history, with a hard-coded fallback
findings.description: The done page should show the reservation just made. Confirm redirects with only ?slot=, so initDone reconstructs the number from all stored reservations: it joins every earlier reservation for the same session ('FT-4471 and FT-4473') while listing only the last one's tools, and with no stored reservations (new tab, cleared storage) it shows the literal 'FT-4471'.

findings.title: Ten-minute basket hold is enforced with no warning or way to extend it
findings.description: WCAG 2.2.1 requires a time limit to be adjustable, extendable or warned about. app.js holds items for HOLD_MINUTES = 10 from the first Reserve and fails Continue after that; the basket page says only 'Items are held for you while you finish', with no duration, countdown, warning or extension.

findings.title: Expired hold shows 'Something went wrong. Try again.' and every retry fails the same way
findings.description: An error should say what happened and how to recover. When the hold has expired, Continue shows the generic 'Something went wrong. Try again.'; hold_started is never reset, so trying again fails identically for the rest of the browser session (only 'Reserve another tool' on the done page clears it).

findings.title: Above 480 px the search form is shown above the results but follows them in tab order
findings.description: On the find page the results section precedes the search form in the DOM; CSS order puts the form first at widths above 480 px, so keyboard focus passes through every result link before reaching the search field shown above them.

findings.title: Results grid minimum column of 330 px exceeds the content width at 320 px
findings.description: Content should reflow without horizontal scrolling at 320 CSS px. .results uses grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(330px, 1fr)); with 16 px page padding each side the content box at 320 px is 288 px, so the single column is 42 px wider than its container and cards overflow horizontally.

findings.title: Tool names on result cards are cut to one line, hiding the words that tell similar tools apart
findings.description: Names that distinguish items should not be truncated. .card__name a sets white-space: nowrap and text-overflow: ellipsis with no full-text alternative; at phone widths the name box is about 200 px, so 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries' and '... one battery' are likely to both end in an ellipsis before the distinguishing words.

findings.title: Fixed action bar on the tool page is not offset, so content and focused days can sit beneath it
findings.description: Content under a fixed bar needs matching bottom padding and scroll-padding. The .actionbar is fixed and 72 px high, but .page--bar reduces bottom padding to 8 px and no scroll-padding-bottom is set, so the end of the page (footer phone number) stays under the bar, and a day button (56 px) brought into view by Tab can be entirely covered.

findings.title: 'Choose a pick-up day first' error is neither announced nor associated with the calendar
findings.description: An error raised on a button press should be exposed to assistive technology. #day-error is a plain paragraph (no role=alert or live region) and is not referenced by the calendar group; focus moves to the first day button, whose name ('Friday 9 October') says nothing about the error.

findings.title: The three-tool limit stated on the find page is not enforced anywhere in the flow
findings.description: The intro says members can reserve up to three tools at a time. Reserve, the basket and confirm never count items, so a fourth tool is accepted and confirmed without a message.

findings.title: Membership and mobile number checks reject common equivalent formats
findings.description: Validation should accept harmless variations. The membership check /^FT-\d{5}$/ rejects 'ft-01234', 'FT01234' and 'FT 01234'; the mobile check /^0\d{4}\s?\d{6}$/ rejects '+44 7700 900123' and '07700 900 123'. Input is only trimmed, not normalised.

findings.title: Tool names on result cards and basket rows are marked up as h2 at the same level as their section heading
findings.description: Items inside a section should be headed one level below it. Result card names are h2 under the 'Tools' h2, and basket rows are h2 with a class 'h3' that has no rule in styles.css, so they also render at the 22 px h2 size.

findings.title: Done page repeats the first tool name in visually hidden text after the tools list
findings.description: Hidden text should add information, not repeat it. #c-tool is an sr-only span filled with the first tool's name, placed directly after the tools list that already contains it, so screen readers announce that name twice.

findings.title: Inline style attributes set spacing outside the stylesheet's tokens
findings.description: Spacing should come from the --space-* tokens. index.html sets style="margin-top: 48px" on the opening-times section and tool.html sets style="margin-top: 8px" on the specs list; the values match the scale but bypass the tokens and the stylesheet.

findings.title: 'Reserve this tool' only adds to a basket, and nothing in view says the reservation is unfinished or leads on to finish it
findings.description: A button labelled with the user's goal should either complete that goal or make clear what remains and offer the next step. On the tool page, 'Reserve this tool' adds the tool to a basket; the only feedback is a toast 'Added to your basket' that disappears within 4 s, the button label stays the same, and the only way on, the header link 'Basket (1)', is scrolled out of view. A first-time member who pressed 'Reserve' has no cue that a session, their details and a confirmation are still required.

findings.title: Search field sits after the full tool list on a phone
findings.description: On a find page, search should be visible near the top. At 375 px the 'Search tools' field and 'Search' button appear after all ten tool cards, about two screens down; the first viewport shows no search or hint of one.

findings.title: Search results update above the viewport with no visible change near the Search button
findings.description: A search should show its result where the user is looking. After tapping Search at 375 px the page stays scrolled at the field; the filtered list changes above, out of view, and no count or message appears near the button.

findings.title: Sticky 'Reserve this tool' is in view before the required pick-up day calendar
findings.description: A required choice should be visible, or announced, before the action that depends on it. On the tool page at 375 px the first viewport shows the sticky 'Reserve this tool' button while the 'Pick-up day' calendar is below the fold; nothing says a day must be chosen first. Pressing it shows 'Choose a pick-up day first.'.

findings.title: 'Choose a pick-up day first.' error stays on screen after a day is chosen
findings.description: An error should clear once it is resolved. After pressing Reserve without a day and then choosing one, 'Pick-up day: Friday 16 October' (or Saturday 17) shows directly above the still-visible red 'Choose a pick-up day first.'; the ARIA snapshot also still contains the message.

findings.title: Basket asks for a pick-up session after the pick-up day was already chosen
findings.description: Users should not be asked the same thing twice. The basket line already says 'Pick up Saturday 17 October', yet 'Pick-up session' radios start unselected and Continue fails with 'Choose a pick-up session' until one is chosen.

findings.title: Pick-up session list runs latest first and includes sessions before the chosen pick-up day
findings.description: Date choices are expected in chronological order and limited to valid options. The list reads Wed 28, Sat 24, Wed 21, Sat 17, Wed 14, Sat 10 October, although the tool's pick-up day is Saturday 17; the first 'Saturday' a scanning user meets is the 24th.

findings.title: Header still shows 'Basket (1)' after the reservation is confirmed
findings.description: After a checkout completes, indicators of pending items should reset. On 'Reservation confirmed' the header link reads 'Basket (1)'.

findings.title: Calendar accepts a pick-up day when the library is closed
findings.description: Members do not know which days are sessions, so the pick-up day control should prevent or flag days when the desk is shut. On the tool page any of the 21 days can be chosen. Choosing Monday 12 October (not marked open) and pressing 'Reserve this tool' adds the drill, and the basket then reads 'Pick up Monday 12 October'. No warning appears at any point.

findings.title: A reservation can be confirmed for a session before the tool is available
findings.description: The tool's 'Available from' date should limit which pick-up days and sessions can be chosen. The pressure washer is listed 'Available from Sat 17 Oct', yet Saturday 10 October can be chosen as the pick-up day. The basket then offers the 10 and 14 October sessions. Confirming produces 'Reservation confirmed' for 'Saturday 10 October, 10:00 to 13:00', with no warning anywhere.

findings.title: Confirm page shows two different collection dates after the session is changed
findings.description: A check-and-confirm summary should state one collection date. After Change > Wednesday 21 October > Continue, the summary's Tools row still reads 'one week, pick up Saturday 17 October' while the Pick-up session row reads 'Wednesday 21 October, 18:00 to 20:00'. The same contradiction appears whenever the session differs from the calendar day.

findings.title: Using Change on the confirm page clears the details already entered
findings.description: Changing one choice in a review step should keep the rest of the reservation, including the form. With membership number, name and mobile filled in, following Change, picking Wednesday 21 and pressing Continue returns to a confirm page with all three fields empty.

findings.title: Search is placed above the tool list on desktop but below all ten cards on phones
findings.description: Search should be in the same, findable place at every width. At 1280 px 'Search tools' sits above the list. At 375 px it comes after all ten cards (about 1,600 px down), just above Opening times.

findings.title: Filter control is an unlabelled icon
findings.description: The persona does not know where the date filter is. The only way into 'Available from' and 'Category' is a square button showing a filter-lines icon with no visible text. Its accessible name 'Filters' is not shown on screen.

findings.title: Pick-up sessions are listed latest first
findings.description: Dates are expected in calendar order. The basket shows sessions from Wednesday 28 October at the top down to Saturday 10 October at the bottom, while the accessibility tree lists them earliest first.

findings.title: Loan-length list does not close with Escape
findings.description: An open list should close with Esc. With the loan-length list open, pressing Escape leaves it open (still showing 'One week' highlighted and the next option beneath).

findings.title: Two styles of availability badge with no explanation
findings.description: Different styling should carry a stated meaning. On the find page, 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' and 'Wed 14 Oct' appear as green text, while 'Sat 17 Oct', 'Wed 21 Oct' and 'Sat 24 Oct' appear as grey boxed labels. Nothing explains the difference.

findings.title: Basket does not say how long tools are held
findings.description: The persona does not know how long the basket holds a tool. The basket says only 'Items are held for you while you finish', with no time limit and no statement that nothing is reserved until confirmation.

findings.title: Date filter's helper text says the opposite of what the filter does
findings.description: The 'Available from' filter says 'Show tools you could pick up on or after this day.' With 17 October set, the list drops the sander (available Wed 21) and wet tile saw (Sat 24), which can be picked up after that day, and keeps tools available on or before it. Members need the wording to match the rule so they trust the result.

findings.title: On phones, session days are marked only by a small dot that the user must decode
findings.description: At 1280 px session days in the pick-up calendar say 'Open'. At 375 px the word is replaced by a small green dot, and the instruction above says 'Days marked Open (a green dot on a small screen) are library sessions', so the member has to read and remember that rule to interpret the grid. Members need the session days to be recognisable on the phone itself.

findings.title: Sessions are shown latest first, the reverse of the calendar and of reading order
findings.description: The basket's session list is shown visually with Wednesday 28 October first and Saturday 10 last, at 375 px and at 1280 px; the accessible order runs Saturday 10 to Wednesday 28, and the tool-page calendar runs forward in time. A member scanning for 'this Saturday' expects the nearest session first.

findings.title: Continue and Confirm give no acknowledgement while the next page loads
findings.description: On the basket, after choosing a session and pressing Continue, the page is unchanged at 0.3 s and still on the basket at 1.0 s; the confirm page arrives between 1.0 and 3.0 s. The button shows no pending state. Confirm reservation likewise shows no change at 0.3 s. The member needs a sign their tap registered.

findings.title: On phones the open loan-length list is hidden behind the fixed Reserve bar
findings.description: At 375 px, opening 'Loan length' drops the list down under the fixed 'Reserve this tool' bar; only 'One week' is visible and the 'Two weeks' option is covered. The member needs to see both choices.

findings.title: Remove takes a tool out of the basket at once with no undo
findings.description: Pressing Remove on the basket immediately empties it ('Your basket is empty') with no undo and no confirmation; the chosen day and loan length are lost and the tool must be found and set up again. The member needs a way back from a slip on a small screen.

findings.title: No way to change loan length or pick-up day once a tool is in the basket
findings.description: The basket line shows 'Pick up Saturday 17 October · one week · deposit £20' with only a Remove control; the confirm page's only Change link goes to the session list. Searched basket/default, basket/errors, confirm/default, confirm/errors: controls found were Remove, six session radios, Continue, Change (to basket), three text fields and Confirm. To switch to two weeks the member must remove the tool and start again from the find page.

findings.title: A membership number typed in lower case or without the hyphen is reported as missing
findings.description: Entering 'ft01234' and confirming shows 'Enter your membership number, like FT-01234', the same message as for an empty field, while the value stays in the box. The member needs to be told the format is wrong (capitals and hyphen) rather than that nothing was entered.

findings.title: The fixed 'Reserve this tool' bar covers focused controls and the open loan-length list on phones
findings.description: Keyboard focus and open option lists should stay visible. At 375 x 812 the tool page keeps a 'Reserve this tool' bar fixed at the bottom of the viewport. When the Loan length button gets focus, most of it sits behind the bar. When the list is opened with Enter, the 'Two weeks' option is completely hidden behind the bar, and it is selected by ArrowDown without being visible.

findings.title: Sticky reserve bar covers the calendar and overhangs the content column
findings.description: On tool, the white action bar sits over the calendar rows and over the 'Choose the day…' instructions in the captures; at 1280 its button extends to x=1264, past the 1184 px content edge everything else aligns to.

findings.title: Tool spec list split into two misaligned label columns
findings.description: On tool, 'Category / Deposit / Available from' use one label width and 'Chuck / Batteries / Weight / Case' directly below use a narrower one, so values start at two different x positions (224 px vs 180 px at 1280).

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench placeholder instead of the tool
findings.description: All ten cards on find use an identical wrench glyph in a pale square as the thumbnail. The slot promises a picture of the tool but carries no information, so cards look like a template with placeholders left in.

findings.title: No brand layer or signature on any surface
findings.description: Across find, tool, basket, confirm and done the identity-carrying elements (type voice, colour use, masthead, imagery) are the public-service-form default; the name sits in bold body text beside a stock wrench glyph. Nothing from the library's own world appears visually.

findings.title: Sessions listed latest first
findings.description: The basket shows Wed 28 first and Sat 10 last (duplicate of F-0028/F-0077/F-0092).

findings.title: Uneven 1 + 5 session layout at desktop
findings.description: At 1280 the first session card spans the full width and the other five share a row, with labels wrapping to three lines.

findings.title: Card titles truncated on phones
findings.description: Both drill names render as 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...' (duplicate of F-0047/F-0122).

findings.title: Search below all cards on phones
findings.description: At 375 the search field comes after all ten cards (duplicate of F-0056/F-0119).

findings.title: Navigation labels wrap to two lines on phones
findings.description: At 375 the nav items wrap as 'Find a / tool', 'Basket / (1)' and 'Opening / times'.

findings.title: Empty bands and half-used columns on basket, confirm and done at wide widths
findings.description: At 1280, basket and done end with the footer well above the viewport bottom and a flat grey band below; confirm fields and the done 'What happens next' box take the left half of the column with the right half empty.

findings.title: Masthead still shows 'Basket (1)' after the reservation is confirmed
findings.description: On done, the nav reads 'Basket (1)' although the reservation FT-4471 has been made.

findings.title: Find page overflows horizontally at 320 px
findings.description: The 320 capture is 346 px wide; tool cards reach the right edge with no margin.

findings.title: On phones the search field sits below all ten tool cards
findings.description: At 375 and 320 the 'Search tools' field, Search button and filter button come after the full list and before Opening times, whereas at 768+ they sit under the intro. The find surface's job is to find a tool, and on the device most members use, the control for that job is a long scroll away. The detector's focus-order jump from the last card back to 'Search tools' is consistent with this.

findings.title: Dark-mode 'Available from' pill drops its tint and goes dim
findings.description: In dark, the green 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' pill loses its tinted background and its text uses a mid-green (#2f7d4a on #1d2622 per detectors) rather than the light dark-theme green used by the Search button, while the grey 'later' pill keeps its background. The availability signal, the find list's most product-specific element, becomes the weakest text on the card in the theme many members use.

findings.title: Tool names truncated with an ellipsis on phones
findings.description: At 375 and 320 card titles are cut to one line ('Cordless drill 18 V, co...' twice, 'Extension ladder 3 m ...'), so the two drills, which differ only by 'two batteries' vs 'one battery', become indistinguishable. Tool names are the content members choose by.

findings.title: Filter panel uses an unthemed native date input in the wrong format
findings.description: The 'Available from' filter is a browser-default date field showing 'yyyy/mm/dd' with a native calendar glyph, beside a native 'All categories' select whose label sits on a lower baseline than its neighbour. The rest of the product formats dates as 'Saturday 17 October' and uses a custom calendar on the tool page.

findings.title: Basket session cards break into an uneven 1 + 5 layout at desktop
findings.description: At 1280 the six pick-up sessions show as one full-width card followed by five narrow cards whose labels wrap to three lines ('Saturday 24 / October, 10:00 to / 13:00'). The sessions are listed latest first, so the earliest session, likely the most wanted, is last.

findings.title: Done page has no focal confirmation
findings.description: 'Reservation confirmed' is an H1 like every other page's, followed by a key-value table in which the reservation number is an ordinary grey-label row. Nothing marks success (no success colour, no emphasis on the number, session and deposit the member must remember). The nav also still reads 'Basket (1)' after confirming.

findings.title: Identity is only the name: no visual lever carries the library
findings.description: Across all five surfaces the only identity elements are the bold wordmark set as body-weight text with a 16 px wrench, and the green. There is no typographic moment, no imagery of the library's room or items, no drawn device. The brief's own material (the membership card the green comes from, the community centre, the volunteers' desk) never appears. Operate mode rules out hero moments, not an identity floor.

findings.title: Pick-up calendar lacks a month label and the toast lands on its header
findings.description: The calendar grid starts at Friday 9 with weekday initials but no month or year heading ('Pick-up day: not chosen yet' sits directly above Su–Sa). In the added state the dark 'Added to your basket' toast is placed over the weekday header row, covering 'We'.

findings.title: Find page overflows horizontally at 320 px
findings.description: Detectors report horizontal page overflow and failed reflow at 320 px on the find page (FUN-05, A11Y-07), along with body text closer than 16 px to the viewport edge in card meta lines (LAY-05). Not in my pre-unseal inventory, which used 375.

findings.title: axe color-contrast: Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds
findings.description: Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds (serious impact). Fix any of the following: Element has insufficient color contrast of 3.07 (foreground color: #2f7d4a, background color: #1d2622, font size: 12.0pt (16px), font weight: bold). Expected contrast ratio of 4.5:1

findings.title: Text contrast below 4.5:1: "Available from Sat 10 Oct"
findings.description: Text "Available from Sat 10 Oct" (16 px, weight 700) has 3.07:1 against its computed background in the dark theme at 320 px; it needs 4.5:1.

findings.title: Weak by APCA, passes WCAG: "Members can reserve up to three tools at"
findings.description: Body text "Members can reserve up to three tools at a time and collect " passes WCAG at 8.33:1 but reads APCA-style Lc 59.5 (advisory floor 75) in the dark theme. Advisory only: consider moving the text token along its ramp.

findings.title: Weak by APCA, passes WCAG: "Category"
findings.description: Content text "Category" passes WCAG at 8.33:1 but reads APCA-style Lc 59.5 (advisory floor 60) in the dark theme. Advisory only: consider moving the text token along its ramp.

findings.title: Weak by APCA, passes WCAG: "Items are held for you while you finish."
findings.description: Body text "Items are held for you while you finish. Choose when you wil" passes WCAG at 8.33:1 but reads APCA-style Lc 59.5 (advisory floor 75) in the dark theme. Advisory only: consider moving the text token along its ramp.

findings.title: Weak by APCA, passes WCAG: "Tools"
findings.description: Content text "Tools" passes WCAG at 7.33:1 but reads APCA-style Lc 57.9 (advisory floor 60) in the dark theme. Advisory only: consider moving the text token along its ramp.

findings.title: Weak by APCA, passes WCAG: "Reservation number"
findings.description: Content text "Reservation number" passes WCAG at 7.33:1 but reads APCA-style Lc 57.9 (advisory floor 60) in the dark theme. Advisory only: consider moving the text token along its ramp.

findings.title: Touch-primary controls closer than 8 px: "Saturday 17 October, open" and "Reserve this tool"
findings.description: On the 768 px touch viewport, the hit areas of these primary controls are 0 px apart (edge to edge); they need ≥ 8 px.

findings.title: Text clips under the text-spacing override in li:nth-of-type(1) > article.card > div.card__body > h2.card_
findings.description: With line-height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2em, letter spacing 0.12em and word spacing 0.16em, text ("Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries") is cut off at 1280 px (scroll 427×50 vs client 390×50).

findings.title: Text clips at 200 % text size in li:nth-of-type(1) > article.card > div.card__body > h2.card_
findings.description: With the root font size at 200 %, text ("Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries") is cut off at 1280 px.

findings.title: Overlapping text: #reserve

ground_truth.description: At 480 px and below the stylesheet reorders the page so the list of tools comes before the search form, and the only way to the 'Available from' date and the category filter is an icon-only button (three lines) that opens a collapsed panel below the list. A member who wants tools for a given Saturday sees ten cards first and no date control, so they are unlikely to notice that filtering by day exists. The document order is form then results, so keyboard focus also runs against the visual order.

A search with no matching tool (for example 'sewing machine') leaves the previous results on the page and shows no message: the status region stays empty and the list does not change. The member cannot tell whether the search ran, whether nothing matched, or whether the old list is the answer.

Tool names are kept on one line and cut with an ellipsis inside the card's text column. At phone widths 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries' and 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, one battery' both read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co…' (at 375 px; a character more or less at other widths), so a member cannot tell which card is the right one without opening each; only from about 480 px does the difference show. The full name is only in the link's hidden overflow.

In the dark theme the 'Available from' badge is a mid green (#2f7d4a) on the card surface (#1d2622), about 3.1:1 for 16 px bold text, below the 4.5:1 that text of that size needs; the light theme passes. Members who use dark mode on their phones get the availability line as the least legible text on the page.

The results grid asks for columns at least 330 px wide; at 320 px the content box is 288 px, so the cards run 42 px past it and the page scrolls sideways by 26 px. The same happens at 200% zoom on a 640 px window.

Every day in the calendar can be chosen, including the days the library is closed; only session days carry the word 'Open' (a green dot on a phone). Choosing a closed day highlights it and the page confirms 'Pick-up day: Monday 12 October'. The reservation is refused three steps later, on the confirm page ('The library is closed on Monday 12 October…'), and the only way back to the calendar is the browser.

Pressing 'Reserve this tool' shows 'Added to your basket' for 1.2 seconds and nothing else changes nearby; the only lasting sign is the basket count in the header, which on a phone is above the fold. A member who looked away, or who reads slowly, does not know whether the press worked and presses again.

The 'Reserve this tool' bar is fixed to the bottom of the window and nothing keeps the page clear of it: the page ends 8 px under the calendar and the footer runs under the bar. A day button that sits in the bottom 72 px of the window counts as visible to the browser, so Tab reaches it without scrolling and the bar covers the focused control: at 768 px wide (900 px tall) the first two rows of days, at 1280 px the third row; on a phone the footer and the desk phone number sit under the bar at the end of the page.

The loan-length list opens as a custom listbox. Inside it, Tab moves to the next option and wraps around, and Escape does nothing, so a keyboard user cannot leave the list except by choosing an option with Enter.

The basket says 'Items are held for you while you finish' but shows no time; the hold is ten minutes from the first item and is kept only in the browser. When it has lapsed, Continue waits 1.2 seconds and then says 'Something went wrong. Try again.', which is not what happened and does not say what to do.

The pick-up sessions are laid out in reverse (row-reverse with reversed wrapping), so the earliest session appears last on screen, at the bottom of the stack on a phone and at the end of the row on a desktop, while coming first in the document. Tab moves from the rightmost card leftwards, against reading order, and a screen reader hears the sessions in an order a sighted member does not see.

'Confirm reservation' stays enabled while the request runs for 1.5 seconds, and nothing visible says that anything is happening. A second press, which is what people do when nothing seems to happen, allocates a second reservation number; the confirmation page then lists two reservations for one visit, and the desk holds the tool twice.

The 'Change' link beside the pick-up session returns to the basket without the chosen session, so a member who only wanted to look at the summary comes back to a basket with no session selected and has to choose again. Nothing says the choice was dropped.

material.reply:
I reviewed the whole reservation flow (find a tool, tool page, basket, confirm, done) on phone and desktop widths in light and dark mode. It isn't ready to open to members yet. The good news is that most of the serious problems come from a few causes, and most of those are small changes.

**Assurance level:** none reached; the target in PRODUCT.md is L3. Basic accessibility checks fail, so even the first level (L1) is blocked: horizontal scrolling at 320 px, a keyboard trap, low contrast in dark mode, content hidden behind the fixed bar, and clipping with larger text. No real users have been tested. "Members would…" below means a predicted problem, not something we watched happen.

## Fix first

1. **"Reserve this tool" doesn't actually reserve anything.** It only adds the tool to a basket. The only feedback is a message that disappears after about 4 seconds, and on a phone the link onward ("Basket (1)") is scrolled out of view. A walkthrough as a first-time member on a phone predicted they would stop here, thinking they were done. Rename the button "Add to basket" and, after adding, show a bar that stays: "1 tool held · Go to basket". *(P0)*
2. **Dates that can't work are accepted.** You can confirm a reservation for a day before the tool is back: the pressure washer, "available from Sat 17", was confirmed for Sat 10. The calendar also accepts days when the library is closed, and that is only rejected at the very last step, after the details are filled in, with no way back to the day. Offer only open session days on or after the tool's "Available from" date. *(P0)* This links to the next item.
3. **Pick-up day and pick-up session are asked separately and can disagree.** The basket asks again, doesn't preselect the day already chosen, lists sessions latest first (which screen readers and keyboards also read in the reverse order), and the confirm page can end up showing two different dates. "Change" on the confirm page also wipes the details already typed. Treat the chosen day as the session, so it isn't asked twice. *(P1)*
4. **The 10-minute basket hold is invisible.** The basket never says how long tools are held, there is no warning before it runs out, and afterwards every retry says "Something went wrong. Try again." with no way out. Show the time left, warn before it expires, offer to extend, and give a specific message if it does expire. *(P0, WCAG 2.2.1)*
5. **Dark mode: the green "Available from" badge is too faint.** It measures 3.07:1 and needs 4.5:1. Its tint is also the same colour as the card, so the badge loses its shape. `styles.css` uses a different dark green from the one in DESIGN.md (#8fd1a8 on #24352c), and switching to that is a one-line fix. Dark mode is what most of your members use. *(P1)*
6. **Phone layout:**
   - At 320 px the tool list scrolls sideways, because of a 330 px minimum column.
   - Tool names are cut to one line, so the two 18 V drills look identical.
   - Search sits below all ten tools, so results change off-screen.
   - With 200% text size, names clip and "Reserve this tool" overlaps nearby text.

   That last one matters given your older members. *(P1)*
7. **Keyboard:** once the loan-length list is open, Tab can't leave it and Esc doesn't close it, so the rest of the page can't be reached. The fixed "Reserve" bar also covers focused calendar days and the open list. *(P0/P1)*

Smaller items:
- Tapping Confirm twice while it's loading creates a second reservation number.
- The date filter's hint says the opposite of what the filter does.
- The header still shows "Basket (1)" after you confirm.
- A membership number typed in lower case, or without the hyphen, is reported as missing.

## Worth keeping

- The confirm page's error handling: a summary that takes focus, links to each field, and keeps what was typed.
- The done page says what to bring and where to go.
- "Nothing is paid online" is stated clearly.
- Search results and "Added to your basket" are announced to screen readers.
- Dates are written the way members say them.

## Questions I couldn't ask you (I went ahead without them)

- **Does a member need to pick a session separately from the pick-up day?** I assumed not, which is why items 2 and 3 are one fix.
- **Is the 10-minute hold a firm rule?** It's listed in PRODUCT.md, so I treated it as fixed and recommend making it visible rather than removing it.
- **Are real tool photos available?** The three design reviewers agreed the site looks plain and generic, because every card shows the same wrench placeholder. That's a polish point, not a blocker.

## How I checked

- **Automated checks:** accessibility (axe), keyboard, layout, contrast and text resizing, across 5 pages, 6 widths, light and dark mode and reduced motion.
- **Independent reviews:** three usability reviewers, a walkthrough as a first-time member on a phone, three design reviewers, an accessibility auditor and a code reviewer.
- **Verification:** every finding was re-checked against the live site before it was kept. Three separate raters then scored severity without seeing who found what, and they disagreed on nothing.
- **Still needs people:** VoiceOver and TalkBack runs, real larger-text and dark-mode use on phones, and a short test with about five members doing the "drill for Saturday" task.

Files are in `.ui-evaluator/runs/20261007-234951-audit-standard/`:
- `report.md` / `report.html`: the full report, 101 findings, each with screenshots and file:line;
- `debrief.md`: the findings grouped by cause;
- `agree-disagree.csv`: a sheet for you or your volunteers to mark.

I can start on the fixes next, beginning with items 1–5, which share their causes.
